body:
## Current execution plan — 2026-10-31

**Type: Feature. Priority: P0.** The original audit below describes earlier CI. Current source has JS-first fast PR profiles, docs-only filters, complete-diff draft admission and source-bound production qualification. Preserve those deliveries and audit the remaining gaps against current source before changing workflows.

### Remaining work

1. Deliver #1486's measured source-keyed build/image reuse and small failure-replay lane. Repeated source compilation and multi-gigabyte transfer are concrete current costs.
2. For each main-only failure after a green PR, preserve a minimal regression and add it to the narrowest relevant pre-merge check: JS behavior for shared logic, schema/policy checks for workflows, or a focused CI-only native check where native semantics/lints cannot be validated by JS.
3. The #1455 handoff documents repeated wider-main compatibility follow-ups; PR #1482 already addresses strict Clippy in shared alias fixtures. Reuse these investigations. Do not file the already-fixed specific policy errors again or mistake a green fast PR for released production acceptance.
4. Keep local development JS-first and selective. Adding focused hosted native checks for concrete gaps does not require local Rust/Docker builds or the full release matrix on every PR.
5. Collect all actionable failures from the current candidate before one coordinated corrective push. Preserve protected-main and superseded-PR concurrency policy.
6. Reduce event fan-out where a conclusively skipped delivery never claimed effects, while retaining failed/cancelled-owner cleanup and scheduled recovery.
7. Measure queue, setup, test, compile, transport, solver and verify time, plus pushes/runs per accepted change, time to first actionable failure and time to fully qualified delivery.

### Acceptance additions

- [ ] A recorded production-only regression fails in its new narrow pre-merge check.
- [ ] The fast lane stays bounded; irrelevant heavy jobs do not start on evidence-only or legitimate docs-only changes.
- [ ] Unknown change classification selects the conservative required checks.
- [ ] Cache hits, skipped jobs and partial fast checks never become native/release execution evidence.
- [ ] A comparable before/after sample shows reduced feedback time and redundant build/transfer cost.
- [ ] No existing native/client/release correctness obligation is removed merely to turn the dashboard green.

**Blocked by:** #1486 for the shared-artifact/latency milestone. Admission-race handling is #1485 and blocked-backlog scheduling is #1490.

---
## Historical requirements and evidence (preserved)

> The current execution plan and acceptance additions above supersede conflicting historical implementation prescriptions and dependency lists below. The historical material records earlier findings; revalidate old claims against current source rather than treating them as new unfixed defects.


## Problem

formal-ai is a big Rust project with a JavaScript and TypeScript implementation. Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.

## Findings

1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.
2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.
3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the "closed js-first loop" is not claimed yet.
4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.
5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).
6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).
7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has "Work in bulk; verify selectively" (~line 510) and "push only after re-reading the issue" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.
8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.
9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.
10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.
11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.

## Requirements

1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.
2. Extend the JavaScript stage to run lint, `npm run test:web`, `js/` and `ts/` tests, the js to ts regenerate-and-diff check and the parity check. It must run on every PR, including Rust-only changes.
3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.
4. Treat `skipped` and `cancelled` upstream results as failure for the Rust gate. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit "unchanged, last green on same tree hash" check.
5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.
6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.
7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.
8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. Include a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, limited `-j`, and pruning of old artifacts.
9. Replace `ubuntu-latest` with `ubuntu-24.04` in all workflows and add a check in `scripts/check-ci-workflows`-style form (as in the JS template) that rejects `-latest` labels.
10. Fix or disable `Self-development status` so it is green on `main` for 7 days. Record the root cause in the case study.
11. Merge or close #887, #652, #646, #644, #643, or comment why each stays open. Add a stale-PR report to the weekly status job.
12. Write `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` with before/after numbers for #1188: pushes, CI runs (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first fully green run, peak local RSS and disk of an agent task. Acceptance: the next large PR shows at most one full Rust run per push group and a green first Rust run after the JavaScript stage is green.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (the standard this issue applies)
- link-assistant/formal-ai#1138 (js to ts to rust cycle, source of `layered-ci.yml`); partly covers findings 1 to 4
- link-assistant/formal-ai#1187 (credentials in workflows; touches `Layered CI` dispatch only, not covering gating)
- link-assistant/formal-ai#1168 and #1169 (pin latest action and dependency versions; does not cover runner OS labels)
- link-assistant/formal-ai#1084 (multi-arch images, CI-CD best practice 13)
- link-assistant/hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template and link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template

---
We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: [Feature][P0] Keep JS-first CI fast and close the gap between PR feedback and main qualification
